According to [3] (document 19980037039, pages 108-108), the result of the workload analysis indicates that the surface mission can be conducted with a minimum crew of five, based on the technical skills required. However, loss or incapacitation of one or more crew members could jeopardize mission success. Therefore, a larger crew may be required to address the risk issues. Currently, the Reference Mission is built on the assumption of a crew of six.

So, the answer is: 5-6 astronauts make up each crew in the 1997 NASA Mars Reference Mission (SP-6107).
